data.title: Pityriasis alba — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pityriasis alba** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What is pityriasis alba?**
- Common, benign, low-grade eczematous dermatitis in children (3–16 y) causing ill-defined, round/oval, hypopigmented, finely scaly patches on face (cheeks), upper arms, neck; minor criterion of atopic dermatitis

**Q2. Aetiology.**
- Atopy and xerosis, sun exposure (more visible after summer tanning of surrounding skin), excessive bathing/soaps, low serum copper, Malassezia/ Streptococcus hypotheses (unproven)
- Hypopigmentation is post-inflammatory — reduced melanin transfer and smaller melanosomes

**Q3. Clinical stages.**
- Early: slightly erythematous patches with ill-defined raised border
- Later: hypopigmented, fine branny scales; multiple 0.5–5 cm patches; asymptomatic or mild itch
- Extensive pityriasis alba — trunk in older children/adults

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Vitiligo (depigmented, sharp border, no scale, Wood's lamp bright), pityriasis versicolor (KOH positive, upper trunk), indeterminate leprosy (sensory loss, nerve thickening — important in India), nevus depigmentosus (stable since birth), post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, hypopigmented MF (persistent, trunk, adults), progressive macular hypomelanosis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, tinea faciei

**Q5. Investigations.**
- Clinical; Wood's lamp (no accentuation like vitiligo), KOH to exclude PV/tinea, sensation testing; biopsy only for atypical persistent lesions

**Q6. Management.**
- Reassurance — self-limiting over months to years
- Emollients, mild soaps, gentle photoprotection
- Mild topical steroid (hydrocortisone 1%) for short periods or tacrolimus/pimecrolimus — speeds resolution
- Extensive/persistent: NB-UVB or PUVAsol (older children)

## Quick spotter facts
- Ill-defined scaly hypopigmented patches on a child's cheeks — pityriasis alba
- Check sensation to exclude indeterminate leprosy

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Hypomelanoses; eczemas). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
